label: 1thread_cpu
hypothesis: Measure per-process Baseline 2B JAX memory + wall on CPU at 1 thread; basis for extrapolating thread/worker scaling.
outcome: Wall 56:15 (3375s), wall_jax_total 3321s (auto-init 2105s, iter1 1016s, iter2 200s). Peak RSS 18.35 GB. Bit-correctness baseline. CPU% 430% with THREADS=1 means XLA saturates ~4 cores internally.

label: 1thread_gpu
hypothesis: Probe GPU VRAM per-process for Baseline 2B JAX and measure JAX-iter speedup vs CPU.
outcome: Wall 25:19 (1519s, 2.22x faster than CPU 1-thread). Iter 1 221s (4.6x faster); iter 2 81s (2.47x faster). Bit-identical Cratio_0/Total_Diff to CPU. Peak VRAM 7.71 GB; host RSS only 2.69 GB. 79% of GPU wall is HARK ref sim (CPU-bound) — that's now the dominant cost.

label: 1thr_cpu_par2
hypothesis: Persistent spawn pool monkey-patch parallelizes eco_ref.solve() in the ref sim auto-init. Expected ~2x ref-sim speedup with WORKERS=2.
outcome: Pool engaged (PIDs visible, CPU% 430->814), bit-identical correctness. But only +15.8% wall (47:22 vs 56:15) and +13% ref sim (1828s vs 2105s) — far below 2x. Cause: 2B JAX cold-start in spawn workers paid INSIDE first solve (= ref sim); only 2 workers fit (17 GB/worker × 3 = swap-thrash). Historical 3.88x was 21 workers x HARK (lighter mem), not 2 workers x 2B.

label: baseline_cache_miss_v2
hypothesis: (historical) full-convergence Baseline 2B serial wall at 4 AD iters; reference point for cache-miss bench.
outcome: wall_jax_total 3101.28s with iter walls [963, 103, 88, 73]. Iter 1 is ~93% of cost across iters 2-4 — solve dominates iter 1, JAX MC dominates after. This is the canonical 'serial 2B Baseline 4-iter' reference.

label: 1thr_gpu_par2
hypothesis: On GPU, persistent spawn pool at WORKERS=2 should give some ref-sim speedup; main risk is OOM at 2x7.7=15.4 GB on a 16 GB GPU.
outcome: 16% SLOWER overall (wall_jax_total 1669s vs 1441s GPU baseline). Ref sim +5% slower, iter 1 +23%, iter 2 +152%. Peak VRAM 16006 MB — within 370 MB of OOM but survived. CPU% only 136% (workers stalled waiting on shared GPU). Different failure mode from CPU 2-worker: GPU is the shared bottleneck, so adding workers contends for the GPU scheduler instead of parallelizing. Bit-identical correctness.

label: 1thr_gpu_4iter
hypothesis: Full convergence Baseline 2B 4-iter on GPU 1-worker; apples-to-apples vs historical CPU serial 2B 4-iter (3101s wall_jax_total).
outcome: wall_jax_total 1601s (1.94x faster than historical CPU 4-iter 3101s). Pattern matches 2-iter: ref sim dominates, then iters get progressively cheaper. Confirms GPU 1-worker as the production single-cell config without surprises.

label: 1thr_gpu_refsim_par21
hypothesis: HAFISCAL_REFSIM_PARALLEL=21 wires parallel_eco_solve into eco_ref.solve() inside _build_init_panels_via_hark_quick_sim. Expected 4× ref-sim speedup → 2.3× total wall (1441 → 625s).
outcome: FAILED — parallel eco_ref.solve completed in 234.8s (4.85× faster than baseline-ish ~1100s) but total auto-init wall was 1157.7s (vs 1138s baseline = +1.8% slower). DIAGNOSTIC: eco_ref.solve() actually solves at the BASE state space because switch_shock_type updates only the economy's MrkvArray, NOT each agent's. The REAL recession-state-space solve happens later in the per-cohort solve_if_changed() loop (line 119), serial × 21 cohorts ≈ 945s. My parallel solve attacked the wrong half. Bit-identical correctness preserved. Step 1 done; the real fix is to reorder (update_mrkv_array per agent BEFORE eco_ref.solve, then set MrkvArray_prev to short-circuit solve_if_changed).

label: 1thr_gpu_reorder
hypothesis: Reorder agent.update_mrkv_array(shock_type) BEFORE eco_ref.solve() so the solve happens at recession state space directly, then set MrkvArray_prev=MrkvArray to short-circuit the per-cohort solve_if_changed() serial cold-resolve loop. Expected: 2.67× total wall.
outcome: BIG WIN on ref sim: 1138s → 215s (5.29× faster). Iter 1 also faster: 221s → 160s (1.38×). BUT iter 2 unexpectedly slower: 81s → 234s (2.9× slower). Total wall 611s (2.36× vs 1441 baseline). Cratio[0] drift 0.01% (0.9909 → 0.9910) because back-transferred eco solution is now from 2B JAX-GPU (recession solve) instead of HARK serial (in original, via solve_if_changed's self.solve() at recession). Iter 2 slowdown mechanism unknown — possibly JAX recompile from changed warm-start. Bit-identicality lost; needs validation for paper-grade welfare.

label: 1thr_gpu_reorder_v2
hypothesis: Repeat of Step 1 reorder fix to diagnose whether iter 2's 234s wall in the first run was reproducible or a one-time JIT compile cost.
outcome: RESOLVED: iter 2 = 97.5s (vs 234s in run 1, vs 81s baseline). The 234s was a one-time JIT compile, not a regression. Total wall 472s (vs first-run 611s, vs baseline 1441s = 3.05×). Step 1's true speedup is 3.05× total wall. Ref sim 214s and iter 1 160s reproduce within 1s of first run. Cratio_0 = 0.9910 reproduces exactly. Step 1 is clean — can stack Step 2/3 on top without worrying about iter-2 regression.
